title: Company cadence, decision ledger & all-hands playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc stitches together three things we need finished before the Q2 company-wide run: (1) a concise set of company-level OKR drafts to present to execs, (2) a lightweight decision ledger for the leadership meeting, and (3) an all-hands playbook (run of show + communications) that productizes the Q/A and follow-ups.

Audience:
- Exec staff, TLs, and PMs for review
- All-hands organizers and comms for runbook ops
- Product + Eng leads for OKR alignment

Top-level constraints and framing (short):
- Keep company-level OKRs to 3 objectives, each with 3 key results. We need tight metrics that map to latency, cost/unit, and customer adoption.
- Messaging: emphasize reliability & predictable economics (our market differentiator) while showing measurable progress on cost controls.
- All-hands length: 70 minutes total, with 10 minute CEO update, 25 minute product highlight + demo, 15 minute customer story + SRE panel, 10 minute operational snapshot, 10 minutes live Q&A (and overflow Slack thread).

Proposed Company OKR Drafts (v0.3) — please comment inline:
Objective A: Deliver predictable, measurable inference economics for customers
KR A1: Reduce average per-token infra cost (hosted + dedicated) by 18% vs baseline Q4 2025
KR A2: Achieve 99.95% request success rate for hosted API across 95th percentile tail latency within target SLOs
KR A3: 3 enterprise customers on Dedicated with committed monthly spend >= $75k each

Objective B: Make rollout + rollback safe and fast for model versions across environments
KR B1: 95% of model rollouts execute with automated canary validations in < 15 minutes
KR B2: Reduce mean time to rollback for degraded models to < 8 minutes via automated fallback policies
KR B3: Ship self-service model pinning and version audit logs to Private customers (GA)

Objective C: Grow platform adoption by developer-first flows and eval-driven quality guardrails
KR C1: Increase active developer API keys (30-day active) by 40% quarter-over-quarter
KR C2: 70% of new integrations use Redwood Optimize suggestions at least once in first week
KR C3: Launch two eval suites and monitor for quality regression alerts on top-5 customer prompts

Quick owner suggestions (assignments for draft KRs):
- A1: Product Optimize + Platform economics (Maya Lin)
- A2: SRE + Serving Runtime (Ethan Brooks)
- A3: Sales & Customer Success (Jordan Kim)
- B1/B2: Release Engineering + Serving Runtime (Priya Narang, Samir to consult)
- B3: Private Deployments product manager (Liam O'Connor)
- C1/C2/C3: Developer Experience + Growth (Claire D.)

Decision Ledger (running list for exec sync — add rows here; record decisions, owner, and follow-up):
- D-2026-01: Adopt 99.95% uptime SLO for hosted API; owner: Ethan Brooks; follow-up: publish SLO page (due 2026-02-14).
- D-2026-02: Prioritize autoscaling improvements on Dedicated pools before new region rollout; owner: Priya Narang; follow-up: capacity test plan (due 2026-03-01).
- D-2026-03: Defer new enterprise pricing tier until A1 baseline hit; owner: Jordan Kim; follow-up: draft customer comms (due 2026-03-15).

All-hands Playbook (draft run of show) — 70 minutes total:
- Pre-read (distributed 48 hours prior): company OKR one-pager, short snapshot deck (10 slides), 2 customer blurbs, all-hands feedback form link.
- Arrival & intro (5m): host + what to expect, anonymous Q&A mechanism (Slack thread #allhands-questions and Slido).
- CEO update (10m): top-level narrative + 3 slides (health metrics, decisions, asks).
- Product highlight + demo (25m): focus on Redwood Optimize improvements + unified inference routing demo; 5 min demo, 10 min product roadmap, 10 min outcomes and metrics.
- Customer story + SRE panel (15m): 7m customer brief, 8m SRE on reliability improvements + what went well.
- Operational snapshot (10m): finance topline, Dedicated capacity status, Private deployment roadmap.
- Live Q&A (5–10m): moderated + capture unanswered for Slack follow-up.
- Close + next steps (2m): where to file feedback and how execs will follow up.

Communications plan & cadence:
- Pre-read: 48 hours before (Ops owner: Claire Donovan).
- Reminder: 24 hours before (Comms).
- Day-of morning: host message with meeting link + anon Q form.
- Post-all-hands: 24 hrs — publish recording, slide deck, FAQ, and Decision Ledger updates; capture action owners and add to Team OKR spreadsheets.

Prep checklist (responsibility matrix):
- Slides: CEO + product + SRE + sales (owner: Ethan to coordinate slide deck bundle).
- Demo: Product engineer (Maya) — dry run with host 48 hrs before.
- Customer permission: Customer Success (Jordan) — get sign-off on script and any redactions.
- Analytics snapshot: Platform Analytics (Liam) — compile 3 charts: tail latency distribution, per-token cost delta, active developer keys trend.

Risk register (top items we should call out):
- Demo flakiness (mitigation: pre-record critical path + live fallback).
- Metric volatility that undermines messaging (mitigation: show range + smoothing, call out known instrumentation gaps).
- Heavy cross-team asks immediately after all-hands (mitigation: include prioritized asks + soft-commit windows).

Open questions / items to resolve before distribution:
- Do we double down on cost narrative (A1) vs reliability narrative (A2) as the primary CEO talking point? (need exec decision).
- Does Customer Success want a separate breakout after the all-hands for enterprise customers?
- Which 2 eval suites should be highlighted as wins in the product segment? (options: latency-preserving quantization, routing-based fallback tests).

Slack + follow-up flows (operational):
- Create channel #allhands-q2-2026 for ongoing action items (owner: Claire D).
- Link anonymous form responses to a shared sheet and auto-tag decisions for the ledger (automate via Zapier: Ops ticket RH-1130).

Appendix: CEO talking points (short bullets)
- We are in the business of predictable inference — not just model access. Customers choose Redwood when they need consistent latency and unit economics.
- Quick wins this quarter: early indicators of cost per token improvements and two enterprise Dedicated commitments.
- What we need from teams: finish the rollout validation work, lock down autoscaling test matrix, and prepare customer-ready materials for Dedicated onboarding.

Appendix: Suggested slides (10-slide skeleton)
1. Title + one-line theme
2. Company health in one slide (3 numbers: MRR trend, active developer keys, SLO compliance)
3. OKR summary (3 objectives)
4. Product highlight + demo snapshot
5. Reliability wins (SRE metrics)
6. Dedicated capacity + sales snapshot
7. Private deployments roadmap snippet
8. Decision ledger highlights and asks from leadership
9. What we need from each team (quick asks)
10. Close + where to file questions

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Claire: ping Ethan for SLO one-pager draft by next Tue.
- Maya: confirm demo runbook and capture a 90s fallback video.
- Jordan: draft customer quote + redaction checklist.
- Priya: surface the top 3 release engineering risks in the pre-read.

How to comment: please add inline comments in this doc or add items to the Decision Ledger above. I expect to iterate v0.4 after exec sync next Wed.

Unresolved items to capture in exec sync agenda (short):
- Primary CEO narrative (cost vs reliability)
- Finalize OKR KR metrics and thresholds
- Approve Decision Ledger entries D-2026-01..03 and any new immediate asks

End of draft.
